summary: All 79 occurrences checked. I is consistently Detransitive in the glossary's terms, including lexical rest with no external agent. Detransitive sense 2 is recovery from bodily distress; III.1 is causative healing. No new stem or numbered sense is required.

Emotional calm has lebo as subject of I ṯniḥ/məṯnəḥ and as object of III maṯnəḥ. The l-suffix in məṯnoḥinalan (78/47) co-refers to the resting subject and alternates with unsuffixed məṯnoḥina in 78/48; it does not establish an external agent.

Preterit can describe a result seen prospectively (24/77); Nomen Patiens marks the rested state. Do not infer different forms solely from German tense. -no/-ina and o-vowel plural variants occur across sources.

Existing quotations are deduplicated, including 11/10, 24/57, 24/77, 24/83, 24/98, 24/128, 24/138, 29/138, 30/149, 47/14, 78/17, 115/283–285 and Talay 1/258 = LB 258. PrS page/line references require concordance, not silent replacement.

116/24 is partially misaligned: the German adds the next verse's stone-reaching. No translation from the flagged occurrence is used. Source variants Wache (13/3), Kühe (PrS 34/65), -lux to a woman (24/83), and m Murde (11/44) are retained rather than silently corrected.

Confirm Nomen Patiens ṯniḥoyo versus ṯniḥo plus copula -yo in Dilo and Falako/36; the separate yo at 115/283 supports comparison, not a reconstruction.
At JTM 5.2/101 does maṯnəḥ lebi request reassurance, cooperation or revenge? 65/441 has an explicit revenge target, but the general collocation should remain broader.
Verify Wache/Woche at 13/3, Kühe/Ruhe at PrS 34/65 and the locative m Murde at 11/44 against the edition. Supply a verse-limited aligned translation for 116/24.
Confirm PrS page/line to text/verse correspondences for existing donkey and command examples before changing their citations.
